sections.html:
Across the water from the city of Charleston, Mount Pleasant fills the east shore of the harbor and the tidal Wando River, all of it inside Charleston County. Its limits are strangely long, stretching about 24 miles northeast along U.S. Route 17 nearly to Awendaw.

That means a Mount Pleasant address might be a historic street by the harbor, a newer subdivision or a lot far up the highway. Flood exposure, school zone and commute all change along the way, and so do prices.

sections.h2: Older homes and the Old Village
sections.html:
People settled here in 1680, and the name Mount Pleasant came in 1803. The Hibben House, built in 1755, is called the town's oldest home.

Housing ranges widely. The Old Village, centered on the Pitt Street Shops, is the oldest neighborhood, and its historic district appears on the National Register of Historic Places. Scanlonville grew from an early African American community founded after the Civil War and has since been annexed. Riverside opened in 1930 and is now a gated community.

If you own an older house near the Old Village, ask the Town of Mount Pleasant's planning staff whether exterior repairs need review before you spend money.

Sitting low beside tidal water, Mount Pleasant puts flood status near the top of every buyer's and lender's list. These points from Charleston County's flood flyer tend to come up at closing:

  • Standard homeowners insurance usually excludes flood damage. Flood coverage is its own policy, bought through the National Flood Insurance Program or a private carrier.
  • If the house is in a Special Flood Hazard Area and the mortgage is federally backed, flood insurance is mandatory.
  • A flood policy typically takes effect 30 days after purchase.
  • Agents sometimes want an elevation certificate. A surveyor, engineer or architect can prepare one when the town has none on file.

Phone the Town to ask which flood zone your parcel falls in and whether it already has an elevation certificate on file. Having that paper in hand heads off a delay.

Charleston County School District runs the public schools, so the first question from many buyers is which zone a house sits in. Wando High School opened in 1973. The town also has Lucy Garrett Beckham High School and Oceanside Collegiate Academy, plus middle schools named Laing, Moultrie and Thomas Cario. Check the district's address lookup rather than a listing description.

The Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge, an eight-lane cable-stayed span that opened July 16, 2005, carries U.S. 17 over the Cooper River into Charleston. Charleston International Airport is about 12 miles northwest, and Mount Pleasant Regional Airport (Faison Field) lies inside the town limits.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Charleston County
sections.html:
Filing happens downtown at the Charleston County Register of Deeds, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200. Weekday hours run 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but anything delivered by hand after 4:30 p.m. will not be taken. The phone is (843) 958-4800, and the staff cannot coach you through the forms.

The deed fee is $1.85 for every $500 of value or fraction of $500, divided as $1.30 state and $0.55 county. Flat recording charges set by the county are posted in a fee schedule on its website.

Certain transfers owe nothing: a deed of distribution out of a decedent's estate, and a quitclaim or corrective deed that only confirms title the grantee already holds without any payment. Each deed travels with an affidavit that states either the value or the reason for the exemption.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and what changes at a sale
sections.html:
Charleston County sends the Mount Pleasant tax bill. Under state law you may pay from September 30 through January 15. Anything unpaid after that date picks up a 3 percent penalty after January 15, then 7 percent more if still open before February 2, then 5 percent more before March 17.

The assessment ratio depends on use: 4 percent of market value for a primary residence and 6 percent for other real estate. Should the buyer not plan to live in the house, or should you have moved out already, the higher ratio can shift how the bill is split on the settlement statement.

Taxable value on most parcels cannot climb more than 15 percent at once, yet that protection ends for property that is sold or transferred. The next owner's bill may therefore look different from yours. The county mails reassessment notices in August; ask the Auditor for the present appeal deadline.

sections.h2: Auditor contacts and the homestead exemption
sections.html: Reach the county Auditor for real estate at (843) 958-4234, or about the homestead exemption at (843) 958-4200, option 4. A new owner files their own legal residence application, and the county advises filing early in the year, before bills are mailed.

Sellers in South Carolina normally give the buyer a written property condition statement using the Real Estate Commission's form. For every listed item, the owner can report personal knowledge or decline to make any representation.

Knowingly giving a false or misleading answer can leave the owner on the hook for actual damages, court costs and possibly attorney fees. Still, the statute leaves room for as-is deals, because the parties may agree on the property's condition. A fiduciary administering an estate, a foreclosure and a written mutual waiver are all exempt.

Title 27, Chapter 50 has the full text. A South Carolina real estate attorney can speak to your own facts.

A standard listing is a poor match for certain houses. In Mount Pleasant, a cash sale gets considered when:

  • Storm, roof or water damage would cost real money to repair before listing
  • The house was inherited and the heirs, living elsewhere, would rather stop paying for it
  • Insurance questions or a missing elevation certificate are stalling a loan-dependent buyer on a flood-zone property
  • The owner wants out of managing a rental

Cash Home Buyers looks at Mount Pleasant houses in their present condition and lays out the numbers in writing. An offer depends on the property. You can hold it against a listing plan before you decide anything.

Reach out with a few basics about the house. Our team goes over what you tell us, and if the property suits us the offer comes back on paper with the reasoning for the figure. Line it up against a listing, and turn it down if the numbers do not work for you.

If you agree, you and the title company settle on a closing day. No bank is involved, so nobody orders an appraisal, and timing hinges mostly on the title search plus any payoffs. Whatever you still owe is paid from your proceeds, and the deed is filed in Charleston County.

Before the first call, find your tax bill, a mortgage payoff figure and any flood or elevation paperwork. Heirs should add the estate papers.

faqs.q: Is Mount Pleasant in Charleston County?
faqs.a: Yes, on the east side of Charleston Harbor. Assessments, tax bills and deed recording for a house there all run through Charleston County.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: Take it to the Register of Deeds for Charleston County, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 200. A call to (843) 958-4800 before you go will confirm hours and requirements.

faqs.q: How much is the deed recording fee in South Carolina?
faqs.a: It is $1.85 for each $500 of value. The state keeps $1.30 and the county gets $0.55. A deed that distributes an estate, or certain transfers with no payment, owes no fee.

faqs.q: Do I need flood insurance to sell a Mount Pleasant house?
faqs.a: Not as the seller. A buyer using a federally backed mortgage on a Special Flood Hazard Area house does need a policy, and since policies usually take 30 days to start, that buyer should ask early.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property taxes on my Mount Pleasant house?
faqs.a: Call the Charleston County Auditor at (843) 958-4234 for real estate bills, or (843) 958-4200, option 4, for the homestead exemption.
